title: Corporate Booking and Reservation Policy
text:
The Corporate Booking and Reservation Policy defines the mandatory procedures for reserving business travel, transportation, accommodations, and meeting spaces across the enterprise:
- **Mandatory Self-Service Portal:** All individual business travel reservations—including commercial flights, passenger rail tickets, rental vehicles, and individual hotel rooms—must be booked directly through the Enterprise Travel Portal (powered by Concur/SAP). - **Prohibition of Direct External Bookings:** Direct reservations made via consumer travel websites, airline portals, online travel agencies (OTAs), or hotel front desks are strictly non-compliant. Bookings made outside the enterprise system will not be reimbursed without a written exception waiver granted by the Corporate Travel Desk. - **Corporate Credit Card Integration:** Bookings executed within the portal are automatically charged to central corporate billing accounts or designated corporate travel cards, streamlining reconciliation and eliminating employee out-of-pocket exposure.

title: Corporate Booking and Reservation Policy
text:
To ensure optimal pricing and inventory availability, reservations must adhere to minimum advance booking windows:
- **Domestic Travel:** Domestic flights, passenger rail, and hotel accommodations must be booked at least 14 calendar days prior to the date of travel. - **International Travel:** All international flights and overseas lodging reservations must be booked at least 30 calendar days prior to the departure date to accommodate necessary visa and security approvals. - **Group Bookings and Room Blocks:** Group reservations involving 10 or more employees or meeting attendees must be initiated at least 45 calendar days in advance. - **Late Booking Justification:** Any reservation initiated inside the mandatory window triggers an automated notification to the Department Head requiring business justification for the short-notice booking.

title: Corporate Booking and Reservation Policy
text:
The booking system enforces tiered authorization rules based on total estimated reservation cost and policy compliance:
- **Tier 1 (Automated Instant Confirmation):** In-policy bookings under $1,500 total value are automatically confirmed and ticketed upon submission without requiring manual manager intervention. - **Tier 2 (Manager Approval Required):** Bookings between $1,500 and $4,000 total value require electronic sign-off from the traveler's Direct Manager before tickets or room reservations are finalized. Approvals must be completed within 24 hours to prevent airfare expiration. - **Tier 3 (Executive VP Approval):** Bookings exceeding $4,000, or any booking that includes out-of-policy selections (e.g., flight class upgrades, premium hotel suites, or bookings outside preferred carrier agreements), require formal authorization from the Business Unit VP. - **Unapproved Holds:** Flight fares placed on temporary reservation hold that do not receive necessary manager sign-off within 24 hours will automatically lapse and be cancelled by the system.

title: Corporate Booking and Reservation Policy
text:
Specialized coordination protocols apply when multiple company personnel attend the same event, customer summit, or team workshop:
- **Group Travel Desk Threshold:** When 10 or more employees are traveling to the same destination for the same business purpose or corporate event, reservations must NOT be made as individual portal bookings. Organizers must submit a Group Travel Request to the Corporate Group Travel Desk. - **Negotiated Block Rates:** The Group Travel Desk negotiates collective group rates, dedicated hotel room blocks, consolidated ground transfers, and group airline ticketing discounts. - **Flight Dispersion Rule:** For operational risk mitigation, no more than 15 company employees (and no more than 3 members of the Executive Leadership Team) may travel on the exact same scheduled commercial flight segment.

title: Corporate Booking and Reservation Policy
text:
Procedures for adjusting existing itineraries after initial ticketing and confirmation:
- **Permitted Modifications:** Itinerary modifications (such as changing travel dates, flight times, or hotel checkout dates) are permitted when driven by genuine business requirements, meeting postponements, or client schedule shifts. - **Employee-Initiated Personal Changes:** Any modification requested for personal convenience is subject to applicable airline or hotel change fees and fare differentials, which must be paid directly by the employee. - **Modification Channel:** All reservation changes must be executed through the Enterprise Travel Portal or via the 24/7 Corporate Travel Agent Desk. Modifying tickets directly at airline ticket counters without Travel Desk notification is prohibited as it causes corporate tracking and itinerary synchronization errors.

title: Travel and Event Cancellation Policy
text:
The Travel and Event Cancellation Policy outlines the procedures, liabilities, and financial implications of cancelling authorized business travel, external lodging, catering arrangements, and corporate events:
- **Authority to Cancel:** Any decision to cancel or substantially modify an approved corporate trip or organized event must be authorized in writing by the original approving manager or event sponsor. - **Duty to Minimize Financial Impact:** Travelers and event organizers have an affirmative duty to cancel non-essential services immediately upon learning of a change in schedule to avoid penalty fees and forfeit deadlines. - **Reporting Cancellations:** All cancellations must be processed through the Enterprise Travel Portal or Corporate Event Management Desk, rather than contacting third-party service providers directly, to ensure corporate credits and refund receipts are properly logged.

title: Travel and Event Cancellation Policy
section_title: Flight Cancellation and Airline Credit Rules
text:
When business flights are cancelled, tickets are handled according to fare class terms and airline contract rules:
- **Non-Refundable Ticket Credits:** Most corporate airfare is booked under non-refundable standard fares. When such flights are cancelled prior to scheduled departure, the remaining value is converted into an airline electronic travel credit (e-credit). - **Ownership of Credits:** All airline ticket credits generated from company-funded travel remain the exclusive property of the company. E-credits must be applied toward future business travel for the same employee within 12 months of the original issue date. - **Ticket Expiration:** Unused airline credits cannot be cashed out or transferred to personal accounts. If an employee leaves the company, unutilized credits are surrendered to the corporate travel pool where permitted by airline rules. - **Rebooking and Change Fees:** Change fees incurred due to bona fide business necessity or unexpected corporate restructuring are fully reimbursable. Change fees incurred due to personal convenience or voluntary schedule alterations are the responsibility of the traveler.
section: Flight Cancellation and Airline Credit Rules

title: Travel and Event Cancellation Policy
section_title: Hotel and Ground Transit Cancellation Rules
text:
Lodging and ground transportation bookings must be cancelled promptly in accordance with vendor terms:
- **Hotel Notice Period:** Hotel reservations must be cancelled at least 48 hours prior to local check-in time (or the specific cancellation cutoff indicated on the reservation confirmation). - **Late Hotel Cancellations:** Cancellations made within the 48-hour window or failure to appear (no-show) incur a penalty charge equal to one night's room and tax. This fee is reimbursable only if caused by medical emergencies, severe weather disruptions, or client-initiated meeting cancellations verified by the traveler's manager. - **Rental Cars:** Rental vehicle reservations through corporate partner agencies may be cancelled up to 24 hours prior to pickup without financial penalty. Same-day cancellations may incur a nominal administrative fee of $25. - **Rail Tickets:** Amtrak and regional rail tickets must be cancelled at least 1 hour prior to departure to receive full refund or travel credit.
section: Hotel and Ground Transit Cancellation Rules

title: Travel and Event Cancellation Policy
section_title: Event Venue and Group Booking Penalties
text:
Cancelling off-site corporate events, workshops, team off-sites, and venue reservations involves substantial contractual obligations:
- **60+ Days Prior to Event:** Cancellations submitted 60 calendar days or more prior to the event start date incur a 10% administrative contract processing fee. The remainder of any advanced deposit will be refunded to the corporate account. - **30 to 59 Days Prior to Event:** Cancellations made between 30 and 59 calendar days prior forfeit the initial 50% contract deposit. - **Fewer than 30 Days Prior to Event:** Cancellations made fewer than 30 calendar days before the event start date result in forfeiture of 100% of the total venue contract value. - **Force Majeure:** Cancellation penalties are waived only under formal force majeure conditions (e.g., natural disasters, government-mandated travel bans, state emergencies) as outlined in the executed vendor contract.
section: Event Venue and Group Booking Penalties

title: Travel and Event Cancellation Policy
section_title: Catering and Food Service Cancellation Schedules
text:
Catering orders for meetings and events carry strict preparation and sourcing deadlines:
- **Full Refund Window:** Catering orders cancelled at least 5 full business days prior to the event date receive a 100% refund of all catering fees. - **Partial Refund Window:** Cancellations made between 48 hours and 5 business days prior to the scheduled service incur a 50% charge of the total estimated food and beverage order. - **Late Cancellations (Under 48 Hours):** Catering orders cancelled with fewer than 48 hours notice require 100% payment of the full order total, as food preparation and ingredient procurement will have already commenced.
section: Catering and Food Service Cancellation Schedules

title: Corporate Catering and Dining Policy
text:
The Corporate Catering and Dining Policy provides financial guidelines and operational rules for providing food and beverages during company-sponsored meetings, training sessions, workshops, client entertainment, and corporate events:
- **Eligible Occasions:** Internal catering may be ordered only for business meetings lasting 4 continuous hours or longer, full-day training workshops, cross-departmental summits, or meetings where working through lunch is essential to operational objectives. Routine team meetings under 4 hours are not eligible for catered meals. - **Client and External Guest Meetings:** Catering is fully permitted for meetings involving external clients, partners, candidates, or vendor negotiations, regardless of meeting length. - **Pre-Approval Requirements:** All catering orders must receive written pre-approval from the host Department Manager at least 7 business days prior to the event date. Orders exceeding $1,000 require secondary approval from the Department Director.

title: Corporate Catering and Dining Policy
text:
To ensure budgetary consistency and fiscal responsibility across departments, all catered food and beverage orders must adhere to fixed per-person spending caps. Caps include food, non-alcoholic beverages, delivery fees, and service gratuities:
- **Breakfast / Morning Refreshments:** Maximum $25 per person (e.g., continental breakfast, pastries, fruit, coffee/tea service). - **Working Lunch / Boxed Lunch:** Maximum $35 per person (e.g., gourmet sandwiches, salads, buffet lunch, hot working lunch). - **Afternoon Snack Break:** Maximum $15 per person (e.g., light snacks, baked goods, bottled sparkling water). - **Casual Evening Reception / Team Dinner:** Maximum $65 per person (e.g., buffet dinner, heavy hors d'oeuvres). - **Executive & Formal Client Dinners:** Maximum $110 per person. Dinners exceeding this cap require written authorization from the Business Unit VP.

title: Corporate Catering and Dining Policy
text:
To ensure food hygiene, quality, and streamlined payment processing:
- **Corporate Preferred Vendor List:** Catering orders exceeding $500 must be placed with approved corporate caterers listed in the Enterprise Procurement Portal. Preferred caterers offer direct corporate master billing, eliminating the need for out-of-pocket employee expense reimbursement. - **External Unapproved Caterers:** If an unapproved external caterer or restaurant is used due to specialty cuisine or geographic necessity, the organizer must obtain a valid Certificate of Commercial General Liability Insurance and Food Safety Compliance from the vendor at least 10 business days prior to the event. - **Direct Invoicing:** Invoices from approved caterers are submitted directly to Corporate Accounts Payable and must include the official event reservation ID and approved purchase order (PO) number.

title: Corporate Catering and Dining Policy
text:
Event organizers are responsible for accommodating diverse attendee dietary needs and avoiding excessive food waste:
- **Dietary Information Collection:** Organizers must collect dietary preferences, food allergies (e.g., gluten-free, nut-free, dairy-free), and religious dietary requirements (e.g., Halal, Kosher) at least 7 calendar days prior to the event. - **Plant-Based Baseline:** For any group catering order exceeding 15 attendees, a minimum of 20% of all ordered meals must be vegetarian or vegan options. - **Final Headcount Lock:** The final attendee headcount and dietary breakdown must be confirmed with the caterer exactly 72 hours (3 business days) before the event. Additions within 72 hours are subject to caterer surcharge; reductions after 72 hours do not lower the invoice cost.

title: Corporate Catering and Dining Policy
text:
The provision of alcohol at company-sponsored events is subject to strict corporate oversight:
- **Permitted Events:** Alcoholic beverages are permitted only at evening social events, celebration dinners, and formal client entertainment taking place after 5:00 PM local time. Alcohol is strictly prohibited during daytime meetings and working lunch sessions. - **VP Approval Required:** Serving alcohol at any company event requires written approval from the Business Unit VP and Corporate Human Resources. - **Service Controls:** Alcohol service must be managed by a licensed and insured third-party bartender or banquet staff. Self-service alcohol stations, open punch bowls, and kegs are strictly prohibited. A 2-drink ticket limit per attendee or a 2-hour maximum open bar service limit is enforced for all company events.

title: Corporate Event and Conference Policy
section_title: Event Planning Timelines and Lead Times
text:
The Corporate Event and Conference Policy sets out requirements for initiating, budgeting, planning, and executing internal and external corporate events, customer summits, team off-sites, and technical workshops:
- **Small Internal Events (Up to 25 Attendees):** Planning must begin at least 30 calendar days prior to the event date. Requires Department Manager approval. - **Medium Events & Workshops (26 to 100 Attendees):** Requires a minimum of 60 calendar days planning lead time, approval from the Business Unit Director, and formal event registration with the Corporate Events Team. - **Major Conferences & International Summits (Over 100 Attendees):** Requires at least 120 calendar days lead time, detailed financial modeling, and formal review and authorization by the Executive Event Review Board (ERB). - **Short-Notice Events:** Any event requested with less than the required lead time requires exceptional approval from the Chief Operating Officer (COO) and is subject to availability of venue resources.
section: Event Planning Timelines and Lead Times

title: Corporate Event and Conference Policy
text:
To optimize corporate expenditure and mitigate legal risks associated with physical venue bookings:
- **Internal Facility First Principle:** Before contracting an external commercial venue, event organizers must check internal company auditorium and conference facilities. External venue booking will only be approved if internal facilities are unavailable or inadequate for the event scope. - **Venue Contract Execution:** Event organizers are not legally authorized to sign venue agreements, banquet event orders (BEOs), or hotel master service agreements. All contracts with a financial commitment exceeding $2,500 must be reviewed by Corporate Legal and signed exclusively by an authorized representative from Corporate Procurement. - **Site Visits:** Pre-event site inspections are reimbursable only for events exceeding 75 attendees and are limited to a single traveling planner for a maximum of 2 days.

title: Corporate Event and Conference Policy
text:
Managing guest lists and participant credentials is vital for physical security and compliance:
- **Employee-to-Guest Ratio:** For recruitment, networking, or client-focused events, an employee-to-external guest ratio of at least 1 employee per 3 external guests (1:3) must be maintained to maximize business impact. - **Guest List Deadlines:** All external guest lists, speaker credentials, and participant rosters must be finalized and submitted to Corporate Security at least 5 business days prior to the event for security badging and visitor clearance. - **Unregistered Attendees:** Walk-in or unregistered attendees will not be granted access to closed corporate events or workshops without on-site authorization from the Lead Event Sponsor.

title: Corporate Event and Conference Policy
section_title: Budgeting, Deposit Schedules, and Expense Tracking
text:
Corporate events must operate strictly within approved line-item budget allocations:
- **Budget Approval:** A comprehensive event budget outlining venue rental, audio/visual (AV) production, catering, marketing collateral, speaker honorariums, and attendee transportation must be approved prior to making financial commitments. - **Standard Deposit Milestones:** Venue contract payments must follow standard corporate milestone schedules: an initial deposit capped at 25% upon contract execution, a secondary 50% progress payment 30 calendar days before the event, and the final 25% balance paid within 30 days post-event upon satisfactory delivery of services. - **Budget Overruns:** Any projected budget variance exceeding 10% of the total approved budget requires immediate resubmission and approval from the Business Unit VP.
section: Budgeting, Deposit Schedules, and Expense Tracking

title: Corporate Event and Conference Policy
text:
Ensuring the safety, accessibility, and well-being of all participants is mandatory:
- **ADA Accessibility Compliance:** All external venues must be fully compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) or equivalent local accessibility statutes, including wheelchair ramps, accessible restrooms, and hearing-assistive AV technology upon request. - **Emergency Action Plans:** Event organizers must obtain and review the venue's emergency evacuation plans, assembly zones, and medical response procedures prior to the event start. - **On-Site First Aid:** For all corporate events exceeding 50 in-person attendees, a certified on-site first aid coordinator or venue emergency medical responder must be designated and available during all event hours.

title: Corporate Lodging and Hotel Policy
text:
The Corporate Lodging and Hotel Policy establishes standards for lodging quality, safety, cost limits, and booking channels for business trips:
- **Mandatory Booking Channel:** All individual and small-group hotel reservations must be booked directly through the Enterprise Travel Portal or the authorized corporate travel management agency. - **Direct Bookings:** Hotel accommodations booked directly on third-party consumer booking websites (e.g., Expedia, Booking.com, Airbnb) are non-compliant and will not be reimbursed unless an official exception waiver is granted in writing by the Corporate Travel Desk prior to the stay. - **Corporate Rate Agreements:** Employees are required to select preferred corporate hotel chains (e.g., Marriott, Hyatt, Hilton, IHG) where discounted corporate negotiated rates and complimentary amenities (such as breakfast or Wi-Fi) are automatically applied.

title: Corporate Lodging and Hotel Policy
section_title: Nightly Room Rate Caps and Tiered Ceilings
text:
Reimbursement for hotel accommodations is subject to nightly room rate caps determined by geographic destination tiers. Nightly caps apply to the base room rate excluding mandatory local occupancy taxes and tourism fees:
- **Standard Domestic Locations:** The maximum allowable base rate is $220 per night. - **Tier 1 Domestic Metropolitan Areas:** In high-cost urban centers (including New York City, San Francisco, Boston, Washington D.C., and Chicago), the maximum allowable base rate is $320 per night. - **International Standard Destinations:** The maximum allowable base rate is $260 per night. - **International High-Cost Tier 1 Metros:** For major global financial hubs (including London, Tokyo, Paris, Geneva, Zurich, and Singapore), the nightly room cap is $350 per night. - **Conference Room Blocks:** If an employee is attending an approved corporate conference or industry convention with an official designated conference room block rate that exceeds the standard tier ceiling, the higher rate is approved automatically provided the reservation is confirmed within the official block.
section: Nightly Room Rate Caps and Tiered Ceilings

title: Corporate Lodging and Hotel Policy
text:
Employees must select standard single-occupancy accommodations when booking business travel lodging:
- **Eligible Room Types:** Standard Queen or King single-occupancy rooms are authorized. Suite upgrades, executive level lounges, penthouse suites, and ocean-view premium rooms are not reimbursable unless provided at zero additional cost by the hotel. - **Complimentary Services and Internet:** High-speed internet access for business work is fully reimbursable if not provided complimentary by the hotel. - **Fitness and Wellness Facilities:** Standard complimentary access to hotel fitness centers is expected; paid premium fitness classes or spa access are personal expenses. - **Room Service:** In-room dining and room service are permitted only if total meal costs fall within the traveler's daily per diem allowance ($85/day domestic, $125/day Tier 1 international).

title: Corporate Lodging and Hotel Policy
text:
Hotels require a valid payment method upon check-in to secure incidental charges:
- **Personal Card for Incidentals:** Employees must provide a personal credit card at check-in to cover all non-business incidental charges. - **Non-Reimbursable Incidentals:** In-room mini-bar items, pay-per-view movies, video games, dry cleaning for stays under 5 nights, and discretionary personal services are not reimbursable. - **Extended Stay Laundry:** For continuous business stays exceeding 5 consecutive nights at a single hotel location, reasonable laundry and pressing charges are reimbursable up to a maximum of $30 per calendar week.

title: Corporate Lodging and Hotel Policy
section_title: Hotel Cancellation Windows and No-Show Fees
text:
To prevent unnecessary financial penalties from unused hotel bookings, employees must adhere to hotel cancellation rules:
- **Cancellation Deadline:** Hotel reservations must be cancelled at least 48 hours prior to the standard local check-in time (typically 3:00 PM local time on day of arrival), or earlier if specified by a specific property's contract. - **No-Show Penalties:** If a traveler fails to check in and did not cancel within the permitted cancellation window, the hotel will charge a one-night room and tax penalty fee. - **Liability for Penalties:** No-show penalty fees resulting from employee oversight or voluntary schedule adjustments without business justification are the personal responsibility of the employee and will not be reimbursed. If a cancellation is caused by unavoidable business emergencies or documented flight cancellations, the penalty fee is reimbursable with Department Head approval.
section: Hotel Cancellation Windows and No-Show Fees

title: International Travel Policy
text:
The International Travel Policy governs all employee business travel originating in or extending to countries outside the employee's designated home operating territory. Due to elevated logistics, cost, and safety considerations, all international trips require rigorous pre-approval workflows:
- **Approval Hierarchy:** International itineraries must receive written pre-approval from both the employee's Department Head and the respective Vice President (VP) at least 30 calendar days prior to the planned departure date. - **Global Security and Risk Assessment:** Before any international booking can be ticketed, the itinerary must undergo a mandatory security screening by the Global Corporate Security Office. Travel to countries flagged as high-risk by government advisory levels requires additional sign-off from the Chief Operating Officer (COO). - **Early Planning Windows:** Last-minute international travel requests submitted with fewer than 14 days notice require executive justification detailing why the trip could not be scheduled in advance.

title: International Travel Policy
text:
Flight class eligibility for international routes is determined by scheduled continuous air travel time (excluding airport layovers):
- **Short-to-Medium International Flights (Under 7 Hours):** All international flight segments under 7 hours continuous flying time must be booked in Standard Economy class. - **Long-Haul International Flights (7 Hours and Above):** For uninterrupted one-way flight segments exceeding 7 continuous flight hours, employees are permitted to book Business Class or Premium Economy. This applies to cross-oceanic itineraries to ensure adequate rest and readiness for business duties upon arrival. - **First Class Restrictions:** First Class air travel is strictly prohibited for all employees, regardless of job title, seniority, or flight duration. - **Rest Days After Arrival:** For international flights involving a time zone transition of 6 or more hours, employees are permitted one non-working rest day upon arrival prior to commencing business meetings. Hotel accommodations for this rest day are fully covered.

title: International Travel Policy
text:
The company reimburses employees for administrative costs directly associated with securing necessary documentation for authorized international business assignments:
- **Visa Fees:** Business visa application fees, consulate appointment charges, biometric processing fees, and mandatory international entry permits are 100% reimbursable upon submission of valid receipts. - **Passport Renewals:** Passport renewal fees are reimbursable if the traveler is required to travel internationally on behalf of the company and has fewer than 6 months of validity remaining on their current passport, or if additional blank visa pages are required. - **Required Immunizations and Medications:** Mandatory vaccinations, preventative immunizations (e.g., Yellow Fever, Typhoid), and prescription travel prophylaxis (e.g., anti-malarial medication) recommended by health authorities for the destination country are fully covered. - **Expedited Services:** Expedited courier and consular processing fees are reimbursable only if the travel request was initiated on an urgent basis at the express request of company leadership.

title: International Travel Policy
section_title: International Per Diem and Currency Conversion
text:
Daily living allowances for international assignments are adjusted based on destination city cost tiers:
- **Tier 1 International Metros:** For high-cost global metropolitan centers (e.g., London, Tokyo, Zurich, Singapore, New York), the international daily meal allowance is $125 per day ($30 breakfast, $40 lunch, $55 dinner). - **Tier 2 International Cities:** For all standard international destinations not designated as Tier 1, the international daily meal allowance is $95 per day ($25 breakfast, $30 lunch, $40 dinner). - **Foreign Exchange Fees:** Mandatory bank conversion fees, credit card international transaction fees (typically 1% to 3%), and currency exchange booth service charges are fully reimbursable when supported by statements. - **Exchange Rate Application:** Expenses incurred in foreign currencies must be converted to local home currency using the historical exchange rate on the date of transaction from the Enterprise Finance Portal or the traveler's official credit card statement.
section: International Per Diem and Currency Conversion

title: International Travel Policy
text:
Employee health, safety, and security are paramount during overseas assignments:
- **Corporate Medical Coverage:** All international travelers are automatically enrolled in the Corporate International SOS medical and emergency assistance program. This policy covers emergency medical treatment, hospitalization, prescription replacement, and medical evacuation to the nearest accredited medical center. - **Traveler Tracking Registry:** Prior to departure, employees must register their complete flight itinerary, hotel address, and active local contact number in the Global Traveler Registry. - **Emergency Incident Protocol:** In the event of political unrest, natural disasters, or severe health emergencies, travelers must immediately contact the 24/7 Global Security Operations Hotline and follow instructed evacuation procedures.

title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
To maintain accurate financial accounting and timely budget reconciliations, all employees must submit expense reimbursement claims promptly:
- **Standard Submission Window:** Expense claims must be submitted via the Enterprise Finance Management portal within 21 calendar days following the conclusion of the business trip or event date. - **Monthly Recurring Expenses:** Continuous expenses (e.g., local transit passes, mobile phone allowances) must be submitted by the 5th business day of the following calendar month. - **Late Submission Grace Period:** Expense reports submitted between 22 and 45 calendar days after the event require written justification and will be subject to a secondary review by the Department Finance Manager. - **Forfeiture of Reimbursement:** Any expense report submitted more than 45 calendar days after the completion of travel is deemed expired and will be automatically rejected, forfeiting reimbursement eligibility, unless an executive exemption is granted by the VP of Finance.

title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
Comprehensive documentation is required for all expense claims submitted to Corporate Accounts Payable:
- **Itemized Receipts:** Itemized digital receipts showing the date, vendor name, specific items purchased, unit cost, taxes, and total amount are required for any single transaction exceeding $25. Credit card charge slips showing only the final total are not sufficient without the accompanying itemized receipt. - **Threshold for Missing Receipts:** For out-of-pocket expenses under $75 where obtaining a physical receipt was not feasible (such as coin-operated parking or small cash tips), an electronic Missing Receipt Declaration Form may be submitted. An employee may utilize this exception a maximum of 3 times per calendar year. - **Digital Image Quality:** All uploaded receipts must be clear, fully legible, and properly rotated. Blurred, clipped, or unreadable receipts will delay claim approval. - **Pre-Paid Corporate Invoices:** Expenses billed directly to corporate master accounts (such as company-arranged group venue deposits) must not be submitted on individual employee expense reports.

title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
All reimbursement claims are routed dynamically through an approval hierarchy based on the cumulative financial total:
- **Tier 1 (Claims up to $1,000):** Requires direct manager electronic sign-off. Approvals are typically processed within 3 business days of submission. - **Tier 2 (Claims from $1,001 to $5,000):** Requires approval from both the Direct Manager and the Department Head / Director. - **Tier 3 (Claims exceeding $5,000):** Requires approval from the Direct Manager, Department Head, VP of Business Unit, and the Corporate Finance Controller. - **Out-of-Policy Exceptions:** Any expense claim containing line items exceeding established policy caps (such as hotel nightly room ceilings or meal per diem limits) automatically triggers an Out-of-Policy audit flag requiring explicit justification and VP sign-off before payment.

title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
For expenses incurred during international travel, the following currency conversion rules apply:
- **Credit Card Billing Statements:** If transactions were paid using a personal or corporate credit card, the employee must attach the corresponding monthly credit card statement showing the exact converted local currency amount and foreign transaction fee. - **Cash Conversions:** If cash was converted into local currency abroad, the currency exchange receipt must be uploaded to substantiate the conversion rate. - **Standard Spot Rate Fallback:** In the absence of an exchange receipt or card statement conversion, the Finance Portal automatically calculates exchange rates using the official OANDA or European Central Bank benchmark rate on the transaction date.

title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
text:
Corporate Accounts Payable processes approved reimbursement batches according to the standard payroll and payment cycle:
- **Disbursement Schedule:** Once an expense report receives all required managerial approvals, payment is issued via direct deposit within 10 business days (or on the next regular bi-weekly payroll cycle). - **Disputed Line Items:** If an auditor or approver rejects a specific line item on an expense report, the disputed line is separated into an inquiry queue. The undisputed balance of the claim is approved and paid on schedule, preventing full claim delays. - **Overpayments and Audits:** The company reserves the right to audit expense reports for up to 24 months post-reimbursement. Any accidental duplicate payment or fraudulent claim will be recovered via payroll adjustment.

title: Corporate Travel Policy
text: The purpose of the Corporate Travel Policy is to establish clear guidelines for all employees undertaking authorized business travel on behalf of the company. Business travel is defined as any journey required for official company operations, client engagements, conferences, or off-site corporate events. All employees, contractors, and authorized representatives are eligible for travel support provided their itinerary is pre-approved by their direct manager. Travel arrangements must balance cost-effectiveness, employee safety, and operational necessity. Pre-approval must be requested and documented through the Enterprise Travel Portal at least 14 calendar days prior to domestic travel departure. Unapproved travel bookings will not be reimbursed and may result in disciplinary action.

title: Corporate Travel Policy
text: All domestic air travel must be booked in Standard Economy class across all regular routes. Employees are expected to choose the most economical non-stop or reasonable single-stop flight option available within a 2-hour window of their desired departure time. - **Flight Duration Exceptions:** For continuous domestic flight segments exceeding 5 hours in duration, employees may select Premium Economy seating with written pre-approval from their Department Head. - **Preferred Carriers:** Bookings should prioritize approved corporate airline partners unless an alternate carrier offers a fare reduction of 20% or greater for identical routing. - **Baggage Allowances:** The company reimburses the fee for one standard checked bag per flight. Excess baggage fees, overweight bag charges, and priority boarding fees are not reimbursable unless transporting specialized company equipment authorized in advance.

title: Corporate Travel Policy
text:
Employees traveling domestically are encouraged to utilize convenient and cost-effective ground transit options:
- **Rail Travel:** Standard coach or economy rail travel (such as Amtrak Regional) is fully reimbursable for short-to-medium distance corridors. Business class rail is permitted only on express high-speed services (e.g., Acela) when standard coach is sold out or when travel time is reduced by at least 90 minutes. - **Rideshare and Taxis:** Ridesharing services (standard Uber, Lyft) and licensed metered taxis are reimbursable for transit between airports, hotels, client sites, and corporate offices. Premium or luxury vehicle tiers (e.g., Uber Black) are strictly non-reimbursable. Daily local rideshare expenses must not exceed $75 per day without prior manager approval. - **Personal Vehicle Usage:** When an employee drives a personal vehicle for business purposes, reimbursement is paid at the standard corporate rate of $0.67 per mile. This rate covers fuel, wear and tear, and insurance. Fuel receipts for personal vehicles cannot be claimed separately. - **Rental Cars:** Rental vehicles are permitted only when public transit or ridesharing is impractical or more expensive. The standard authorized vehicle category is Intermediate / Compact Sedan. Upgrades to SUVs or minivans require prior approval and must accommodate three or more traveling colleagues or substantial cargo.

title: Corporate Travel Policy
section_title: Per Diem and Daily Meal Allowances
text:
Business travelers are eligible for a daily meal allowance intended to cover reasonable food and beverage costs incurred during travel:
- **Standard Domestic Per Diem:** The standard domestic daily meal allowance is $85 per day, allocated as follows: Breakfast ($20), Lunch ($25), and Dinner ($40). - **Receipt Submission:** Travelers claiming the per diem rate do not need to provide itemized receipts for individual meals under $25, but total daily expenses must remain within the $85 threshold. Any single meal expense exceeding $50 requires an itemized digital receipt. - **Single-Day Travel:** Travel that does not include an overnight stay is not eligible for full per diem; only lunch up to $25 may be reimbursed if the workday exceeds 8 hours outside the home office. - **Alcoholic Beverages:** Personal alcoholic beverages are not eligible for reimbursement under standard travel per diem. Moderate alcohol expenses may only be claimed during approved client entertainment meals in compliance with corporate entertainment guidelines.
section: Per Diem and Daily Meal Allowances

title: Corporate Travel Policy
text:
The company will not reimburse personal expenses incurred during business trips. Non-reimbursable items include, but are not limited to:
- Traffic citations, parking violation fines, and toll road penalties resulting from driver negligence. - Airline seat selection upgrade fees, in-flight Wi-Fi for personal use, in-flight entertainment, and lounge day passes. - Personal side-trips, extended vacation days before or after business travel, and travel expenses for spouses, family members, or personal companions. - Personal grooming, spa services, fitness center day passes, hotel pay-per-view movies, mini-bar refreshments, and hotel dry cleaning for trips lasting fewer than 5 consecutive days. - Lost, damaged, or stolen personal belongings (employees should rely on personal or credit card travel insurance).
